objectReview.assessment: Fixed source distribution, endpoint-only work, zero closed-path electrostatic work and the energy-conservation caveat for time-dependent fields are retained.
Electric-force-only A equals minus the potential-energy change with the same zero; equation (8-22) is not extended beyond its uniform-field model.
Common zero, sufficiently small test charge, unchanged source distribution, signed proportionality, nonzero denominator and applicability to uniform and nonuniform electrostatics are explicit.
Potential energy divided by signed nonzero charge, the unit-positive-charge interpretation and exclusion of kinetic/total energy are all correct. The definition's strong-emphasis opener is displaced.
Definition lead-in is faithfully translated without adding a claim or task.
U=E_P/q and equation number (8-23) are unchanged; preceding prose supplies the nonzero signed-q condition.
Vector field strength describes force and direction; scalar potential determines potential energy given charge and a chosen zero.
Parallel-plate uniform model, neglected edges, negative-plate zero, normal distance toward the positive plate and field magnitude preserve the conditions for U=Ed.
U=E_P/q=Ed and equation (8-24) are unchanged and remain scoped by the preceding model.
All potentials gain the same constant when zero changes; their differences are invariant, while chosen-reference potential values remain usable.
E_P=qU and the same-charge initial-to-final movement lead-in are retained.
Equation (8-25) retains unnumbered initial E_P, explicitly explains it and final E_{P_2}, and preserves the dependence of work sign on both signed charge and potential change.
Delta U=U_2-U_1 is final minus initial; this lesson's potential difference is explicitly the reverse order for the same endpoints.
V=U_1-U_2=-Delta U and equation (8-26) are unchanged.
Potential difference is called voltage, has the opposite sign to the specified potential change, and reverses sign when endpoint order reverses.
Use in current studies is restricted to electrostatically modeled circuit sections and not generalized to total work in induction-affected circuits.
The derivation lead-in retains references (8-25) and (8-26) without new assumptions.
V=U_1-U_2=A/q and equation (8-27) are unchanged.
Electric-force work divided by signed nonzero q uses specified endpoints, fixed sources and negligible disturbance, and excludes other-force work.

The lighting example is an electrostatic circuit section with node ordering and per-unit-positive-charge work; internal source-force and induced closed-loop work are not conflated with electrostatic work.
The potential-difference unit follows work and charge units via (8-27).
SI joule and coulomb, positive 1-coulomb charge, +1-joule electric-force work in the specified order, and the volt definition are faithful.
Historical electrostatic potential-difference unit follows 1 erg per positive electrostatic charge unit; SI and historical numerical values must be converted before combining.
The source's approximate conversion factor is explicitly retained rather than represented as an exact modern definition.

The conversion retains 1, 10^7, 3 times 10^9 and 1/300 with the same operators and fractions, localizes only unit-name text literals, and explicitly warns that the limited digits are not an exact definition.
